title: Motion for a further extension of time to file respondent's brief on the merits

pages.text:
William M. Jay
+1 202 346 4190
WJay@goodwinlaw.com
Goodwin Procter LLP
1900 N Street, N.W.
Washington, D.C. 20036

goodwinlaw.com
+1 202 346 4000

January 2, 2026
Ms. Denise J. McNerney, Merits Cases Clerk
Supreme Court of the United States
One First Street, N.E.
Washington, DC 20543

Re: Keathley v. Buddy Ayers Construction, Inc., No. 25-6

Dear Ms. McNerney:

Pursuant to Supreme Court Rule 30.4, respondent respectfully requests a 7-day extension
for its brief on the merits in the above-captioned case.
The Court previously granted an 8-day extension, to and including January 20, 2026.
With the requested extension, respondent’s brief would be due January 27, 2026.  The case
would be fully briefed in time for the Court’s March sitting.
The additional time is justified by a number of professional commitments on the part of
respondent’s counsel, in addition to family commitments and travel during the holiday period.  In particular, respondent’s counsel of record is responsible for an oral argument in a
federal court of appeals on January 5, 2025.
Counsel for petitioner does not object to this further extension of time.
If you have any questions, please contact me at (202) 346- 4190. Thank you as always for
your assistance.

cc: Gregory G. Garre, Counsel for Petitioner
Respectfully,



William M. Jay
